An unstable weather pattern will bring scattered showers and 
isolated thunderstorms tonight for the Marianas, becoming numerous 
by tomorrow. Higher rainfall totals are expected tonight for Guam 
and decreasing northward due to proximity to Invest 97W. Starting 
Monday night, high-end scattered showers and isolated thunderstorms 
are possible for the rest of the week. As 97W shifts north and 
elongates, winds will turn from east-southeast to southwest by 
Tuesday. If 97W manages to develop northeast of the Marianas from 
the ongoing southerly wind burst near Chuuk, then stronger monsoonal
westerlies could occur over the Marianas. However, this remains 
unlikely and forecasted winds remain at 15 to 20 mph for now 
beginning Tuesday. 

Marine...
Gentle to moderate winds will be from the east-southeast tonight,
becoming southeast by tomorrow, and turning to southwest by 
Tuesday. The westerly swell from Typhoon Bavi continues to diminish 
with combined seas at 6 to 7 feet tonight. A moderate risk of rip 
currents and for lightning remains in effect for all reefs for the 
whole forecast period. A new southwesterly swell will start to build 
in starting Monday. How quickly remains uncertain and will depend on 
the strength and track of Invest 97W. This will be monitored closely.

Tropical Systems...
Invest 97W is located at 9.5N 142E and remains broad and 
disorganized with very little convection near the center. JTWC has 
it rated as "low" for development, meaning development is not 
expected within 24 hours. However, scattered to widespread showers 
and isolated thunderstorms surround all sides and are associated 
with winds of 20 to 25 knots. Models indicate the system is expected
to continue west- northwest between Yap and Guam. However, a new 
circulation may form from the southerly wind burst which may shift 
the location of 97W if it manages to consolidate. Either way, 97W is
expected to become elongated as it interacts with the stationary 
boundary to it's north. Residents in Palau, Yap, Chuuk, and the 
Marianas can expect elevated seas and continued showers and isolated 
thunderstorms. These areas should continue to monitor this system 
for further development.

Invest 98W is located at 8.4N 170.6E and appears to have become more
disorganized today as very little convection is present this evening
over or around the center. JTWC has it rated as "low" for 
development. However, some slow development is still possible over 
the next few days so residents in Kwajalein, Kosrae, Pohnpei, and 
Chuuk should continue to monitor this system as it moves west. 
Increased showers and isolated thunderstorms, as well as gusty winds 
and elevated surf could pose a risk to these areas. 

Eastern Micronesia...
Satellite imagery shows widespread cloud cover across much of eastern
Micronesia late this afternoon. Scattered to numerous showers and 
isolated thunderstorms are observed and this will likely continue 
into tonight, so kept the numerous shower coverage in the forecast 
for tonight. Satellite imagery also shows Invest 98W as a broad
circulation near Majuro and slowly trekking to the west. The 
disturbance continues to be rated "low" by the Joint Typhoon Warning
Center, meaning no development is expected during the next 24 hours.
Ensemble guidance supports some development for 98W over the next 
couple of days as it drifts generally westward, but we'll continue to
monitor the invest for any development. Please see the Tropical 
Systems section for additional details on 98W. Increasing shower and 
thunderstorm chances will accompany the disturbance as it slowly 
moves westward with an eventual turn to the north forecast for mid to
late week. 

Light and variable winds at Pohnpei will become north to northeast
during the day on Monday and increase ahead of Invest 98W. North to 
northeast winds will generally prevail at Kosrae as Invest 98W 
approaches through early this week. Light and variable winds at 
Majuro will become south to southeast starting Monday night as 
Invest 98W treks westward and away from the atoll. Wind speeds are 
currently forecast to be gentle to moderate through early this week
at all sites. Combined seas of 5 to 6 feet will continue through 
early this week with seas consisting of a west swell at Kosrae and 
Pohnpei and an east swell at Majuro. A small, south to southeast 
swell is present throughout all waters. Otherwise, locally choppy 
seas will be possible in the vicinity of Invest 98W as it treks 
generally westward.

Western Micronesia...
The High Surf Advisory has been extended through Sunday afternoon at
Yap, and a new Small Craft Advisory was issued for Yap.
